sentences.text: The name Graciliceratops translates to 'slender horned face', a title reflecting the creature's delicate physical construction.
The holotype skull measures approximately 20 centimeters, and unfused vertebrae indicate the individual was a juvenile when it died.
Scientists recognize this species by its fragile frill, a specific tibial-femoral ratio of 1.2:1, and well-developed squamosal processes.
The femur is 9.5 centimeters long, lightly curved with a large head and a fragile fourth trochanter located above the midlength.
The tibia measures 11 centimeters, is larger than the femur, and features a more developed proximal articulation than the distal end.
Its toe claws are dorsoventrally flattened and somewhat sharply developed.
This juvenile specimen is estimated to be 60 centimeters long and weigh between 2.27 and 9.1 kilograms.
The frill features large openings bounded by very slender struts, a structure similar to that of later Protoceratops.
Adult Graciliceratops is estimated to have reached about 2 meters in length, similar to Protoceratops.
In 1975, Teresa Maryańska and Halszka Osmólska described the specimen as belonging to the genus Microceratops.
Paul Sereno later argued that the original genus Microceratops was a nomen dubium due to unjustified referrals and lack of diagnosis.
Like other ceratopsians, Graciliceratops was likely a herbivore that used a powerful beak and cutting teeth to process tough plant matter.
Because angiosperms were geographically limited during the Cretaceous, it is deduced that Graciliceratops fed on ferns, cycads, and conifers.
The shape of its beak suggests it was used to bite leaves and thorns.
Fossilized fruits found in the formation suggest the existence of angiosperm plants in the environment.
Phylogenetic analysis identifies Graciliceratops as a basal neoceratopsian.
Graciliceratops is classified within the family Protoceratopsidae.
Graciliceratops lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous period.
The animal lived approximately 90 million years ago during the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Asia.
The Shireegiin Gashuun locality is likely from the early Late Cretaceous, older than the Djadokhta Formation where Protoceratops was found.
The time range for Graciliceratops is estimated from the Cenomanian to the Santonian, between 100.5 and 83.6 million years ago.

Graciliceratops lived alongside diverse contemporaries including the dromaeosaurid Achillobator, tyrannosauroid Khankhuuluu, therizinosaurs, pachycephalosaurs, ornithomimosaurs, ankylosaurs, the sauropod Erketu, and the hadrosauroid Gobihadros.
It is debated whether the original classification of the specimen as Microceratops was valid, with Sereno considering it a nomen dubium.
